# Psalm 111 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart, in the company of the upright, in the congregation.

**2** Great are the works of the LORD, studied by all who delight in them.

**3** Full of splendor and majesty is his work, and his righteousness endures forever.

**4** He has caused his wondrous works to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and merciful.

**5** He provides food for those who fear him; he remembers his covenant forever.

**6** He has shown his people the power of his works, in giving them the inheritance of the nations.

**7** The works of his hands are faithful and just; all his precepts are trustworthy;

**8** they are established forever and ever, to be performed with faithfulness and uprightness.

**9** He sent redemption to his people; he has commanded his covenant forever. Holy and awesome is his name!

**10** The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; all those who practice it have a good understanding. His praise endures forever!

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 111.

- **111:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **111:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **111:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **111:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **111:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **111:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **111:1-10**: An acrostic psalm — each half-verse begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet (aleph through tav).
- **111:10**: 'The-beginning-of wisdom the-fear-of YHWH' — the foundational wisdom saying, shared with Proverbs 9:10 and Job 28:28.

### LOGOS
- **111:1-10**: A perfect acrostic paired with Psalm 112 — 111 praises God's character, 112 describes the godly person who mirrors it.
- **111:10**: The wisdom climax: fear of YHWH is not terror but reverent awe — the proper posture before the God described in vv. 1-9.

### PNEUMA
- **111:2**: 'Everyone who loves them explores them deeply' — this psalm invites curiosity about God. Studying God's works isn't boring — it's the most rewarding research project in existence.
- **111:10**: The most famous wisdom saying in the Bible: 'Reverence for the LORD is where wisdom begins.' Not IQ, not education, not experience — reverence. Everything else builds on that foundation.

— SOPHIA
